instrucciones:
Recibes registros de una base de reglas de producción audiovisual con IA. Cada registro trae su texto
literal completo, el documento y la ruta de encabezados donde está, y a veces un contexto (encabezado de tabla o de
bloque). El encabezado dice el alcance: modelo, régimen, etapa, caso. Para CADA registro devuelve:
- "enunciado": la regla en español, UNA frase: qué exige, prohíbe, limita o especifica. Si es un ejemplo o una
  explicación sin norma, empieza con "Ejemplo:" o "Explicación:".
- "alcance": a qué aplica exactamente según texto y encabezado (modelo y versión, caso, etapa, régimen) o "general".
- "temas": de 1 a 3 claves de la lista, las que mejor describen de qué trata.
Lista de temas (clave: descripción):

estrategia_conceptos: brief, SMP, territorios, concept cards, matriz, dirección narrativa
guion_formato: guion: sluglines, acción, personajes, diálogo, XML, estructura, escenas

Devuelve JSON {"registros": [{"id": "...", "enunciado": "...", "alcance": "...", "temas": ["..."]}]} con

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline

registros.texto:
Three exceptions:
- Seedance — 2-3 shots inside one 5-10s clip via "Cut to" syntax (see `seedance.md` §8).
- Kling 3.0 — up to 6 shots inside one generation, up to 15s, with native audio and dialogue (see `kling.md` §3).
- Seedance 2.5 — up to 30s in one pass. The working structure is consecutive stages, each with one primary state change and an explicit visible end state (see `seedance-25.md` §6).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 12. U11. The final image rule

registros.texto: Every clip needs a clear final frame. The model uses the ending as emotional destination.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 12. U11. The final image rule

registros.texto: - "Ends on his face frozen in the blue refrigerator light" beats "he stands there sadly."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 12. U11. The final image rule

registros.texto: The final image is also one of the five anchors (see `dramaturgy.md` §13). Naming it is non-negotiable.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)

registros.texto:
Before returning the final prompt to the user, audit every shot. Each shot must carry at least one of each:

1. Environmental pressure (lighting, weather, surface, sound of the room).
2. Physical micro-action on the body (jaw, hand, breath, eye, gesture).
3. Sound anchor or recurring visual motif tied to the emotional spine.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)

registros.texto: If a shot has zero, fix it before sending. If a shot has only one, ask whether you can make it two without bloat. The strongest prompts in this skill's worked examples always have all three.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)

registros.texto: Empty descriptors that fail this check: "establishing wide shot", "beautiful lighting", "dynamic camera move", "cinematic look", "intense moment", "dramatic close-up". Replace each with three concrete physical facts.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline

registros.texto: Wherever a model accepts reference assets (Seedance `@Image/@Video/@Audio`, Kling Element Binding and Omni references, Veo ingredients), **every asset gets an explicit role written in the prompt**: what it defines (appearance, motion, voice, scene, camera path) and what to ignore ("Do not use the image background", "Do not use the people in the image").

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline

registros.texto: - Bind each subject individually: "<Character A> corresponds to @Image 1 — use only the appearance, hairstyle, and clothing." Never the collective form "@Images 1 through 4 define four characters respectively" — it does not state which is which.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline

registros.texto: - Do not restate what a reference already defines. If a video reference carries the motion, name only the attributes to inherit; re-describing every action fights the reference.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline

registros.texto: - More assets is not more control. Control comes from role clarity; unassigned assets bleed into the frame.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline

registros.texto: Model-specific limits and templates live in the model files (`seedance-25.md` §5 has the fullest system).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration

registros.texto:
When a prompt is overloaded (10+ scenes, many subjects, spatial tricks), adding more description makes it worse. Instead, declare priorities — the model cannot know what matters most unless told what to protect and what to sacrifice:

1. The core subject that must survive every shot.
2. The key shots that must appear.
3. The transitions where the model may freestyle.
4. The mandatory final frame.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration

registros.texto: This ranks above prompt-length discipline: a shorter prompt with declared priorities beats a longer one without them.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 1. What Veo is

registros.texto: Google's cinematic video model with NATIVE synchronized audio. The only major generator that creates dialogue, SFX, and music in sync with the video and does lip-sync natively. Best for commercial polish, narrative with dialogue, and cinematic audio.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 2. Versions and specs

registros.texto: - Veo 3. Text-to-video, native audio, 4 / 6 / 8 second clips.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 2. Versions and specs

registros.texto: - Veo 3.1. Adds image-to-video with First Frame, improved audio, reference ingredients, stronger motion coherence.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 2. Versions and specs

registros.texto:
Duration. 4, 6, or 8 seconds.
Dialogue budget. Max 8 seconds of spoken audio per clip.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 3. Prompt structure and length

registros.texto: Order matters. Lead with subject and camera. Quality modifiers go at the end.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 3. Prompt structure and length

registros.texto:
```text
[Subject / Action]
+ [Environment / Setting]
+ [Camera / Shot Type / Lens]
+ [Lighting / Atmosphere]
+ [Style / Quality]
+ [Audio]
+ [Duration]
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 3. Prompt structure and length

registros.texto:
Sweet spot. 50-200 words.

- Shorter prompts = more creative latitude, less control.
- Longer prompts = tighter control, higher risk of contradictions.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical)

registros.texto: Veo is the only model that renders synced lip movement and voice. The syntax matters.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Required format

registros.texto: Double quotes + lead-in verb (says, whispers, shouts, mutters, asks).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Required format

registros.texto:
```text
A woman says, "Welcome to the future."
He whispers, "Don't move."
She shouts, "Get out!"
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Required format

registros.texto: Colon after the lead-in verb works too and is often more reliable.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Required format

registros.texto:
```text
A woman says: "Welcome to the future."
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Voice character modifiers

registros.texto:
Place modifiers before the lead-in verb.

```text
He says in a weary voice, "We are fine. We are fine."
She whispers nervously, "I don't want to be here."
He shouts excitedly, "We did it!"
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Timing rule

registros.texto: Maximum 8 seconds of spoken audio. Cram too many words into a 5s clip and the delivery speeds up unnaturally. Cut the line until it fits.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 5. SFX syntax

registros.texto:
Three supported formats. Mix as needed.

```text
SFX: thunder cracks in the distance
Audio: rain on tin roof, distant traffic, one slow breath
(a loud thunderclap)
(key turning in a lock)
(wet footsteps on concrete)
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 5. SFX syntax

registros.texto: Use labels `Audio:`, `Says:`, `SFX:` to separate sound direction from visual direction. The model needs an explicit signal that audio should be generated.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique)

registros.texto: Veo parses structured JSON. This prevents "concept bleed" where describing mood accidentally changes object colors. Use JSON for complex scenes with strict continuity needs.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › Full schema
Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON

registros.texto: - Multiple scenes in one generation.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON

registros.texto: - Strict character continuity across shots.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON

registros.texto: - Complex props that must stay the same color and size.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON

registros.texto: - When a prose prompt kept changing subject colors when you added mood words.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON

registros.texto: Not every Veo prompt needs JSON. For simple clips, prose is faster and often better.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)

registros.texto: Uses the static image as First Frame. Prompt guides motion and sound.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)

registros.texto:
Rules.

- Do not re-describe static elements.
- Describe only motion, camera, light change, and audio.
- Add "maintain the subject from the first frame" to protect identity.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)

registros.texto:
Example.

```text
Maintain the subject from the first frame. Slow push-in, 50mm. She exhales, her eyes shift to the left, one strand of hair falls across her forehead. Warm rim light grows stronger.

Audio: soft breath, distant traffic, one door closing in the next room.
Duration: 6 seconds.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 8. Reference ingredients (3.1)

registros.texto: Upload multiple reference images (character, location, prop) and tag them in the prompt.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 8. Reference ingredients (3.1)

registros.texto:
```text
The character from reference_1 walks into the location from reference_2 holding the object from reference_3.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 8. Reference ingredients (3.1)

registros.texto: Use when you need a specific character in a specific place with a specific object.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Dialogue speeds up unnaturally

registros.texto: Fix. Cut the line to fit 8 seconds of natural speech. Test by reading aloud.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Audio missing from output

registros.texto: Fix. Add explicit `Audio:`, `SFX:`, or `Says:` labels. Do not assume the model will infer audio from visual description.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Camera direction ignored

registros.texto: Fix. Lead the prompt with camera. "Wide aerial shot" at the start beats "cinematic camera work" in the middle.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Character color changes when mood words are added

registros.texto: Fix. Switch to JSON prompt. Lock the character description in the continuity block. Keep mood in global_style where it cannot bleed into object colors.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Lip-sync off

registros.texto: Fix. Check the lead-in verb. "She says, ..." outperforms just quoted speech alone. Colon form often more reliable than comma.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Prompt too long, model cherry-picks

registros.texto: Fix. Compress to the 50-100 word range. Or switch to JSON which handles length better because of structural separation.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 10. Skeleton › Prose version

registros.texto:
```text
[Subject performing action] in [environment]. [Camera framing + lens + movement]. [Lighting direction + color temperature]. [Style + mood + palette].

Audio: [ambient sounds, SFX, music texture].
Says: [character] says, "[dialogue, max 8 seconds of speech]."
SFX: [punctual sound events].

Duration: [4 / 6 / 8] seconds.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 10. Skeleton › JSON version

registros.texto: See section 6. Copy the schema and fill in.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 10. Skeleton › Worked example. Commercial hero shot

registros.texto:
```text
A woman in a cream silk blouse stands in front of a morning window, lifting a ceramic coffee cup to her lips. Medium close-up, 85mm, slow push-in. Warm window key from frame-left, soft bounce fill from frame-right. Cinematic naturalism, creamy palette, shallow depth of field.

Audio: distant city ambience, ceramic clink, one slow breath.
Says: She whispers to herself, "One more minute."
SFX: (spoon tapping ceramic at 2 seconds).

Duration: 6 seconds.
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: frontmatter › description

registros.texto: description: Critique a generated image against its source storyboard shot and prompt, producing revision notes. Use when the user has generated an image and wants feedback before committing. Triggers on "does this match the brief", "review this render", "is this on-brand", "what should I change", or uploading an image alongside a shot ID. The QA loop for AI visuals. Works even without a storyboard-architect run. Pairs with storyboard-architect upstream, visual-prompt-forge sibling.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic

registros.texto: You are the editorial second-eye on AI-generated images. Most teams don't have one, they generate, glance, accept, and ship. This skill is the structured review pass that catches what a tired creator misses.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic

registros.texto: The output is a critique with concrete, actionable revision notes. Not vibes. Not "looks good." Specific, prompt-level or post-level fixes.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use

registros.texto:
Trigger when the user:

- Uploads or links a generated image with a question about quality
- Asks "does this match the storyboard"
- Says "review this render", "is this on-brand", "what should I change"
- Has a generated image and a `shots.json` shot reference and wants QA
- Has a generated image and just wants editorial feedback (no storyboard reference)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce

registros.texto: **Two artifacts from every review, always both:** a human-readable markdown critique (the primary surface) and a machine-readable critique JSON (so a pipeline can gate on the verdict instead of parsing prose). The JSON is detailed in Step 6; it never replaces the markdown.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce

registros.texto:
The JSON goes to `output/critiques/round-{N}/{shot_id}.critique.json`. One file per shot
per round, never a shared filename. A 12-shot project reviewed over three rounds writes 36
critiques; when they all went to `output/critique.json` it kept one, and which one depended
on review order.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce

registros.texto:
The markdown critique uses these sections:

```
## Verdict
ACCEPT / REVISE / REJECT, one line

## What's working
2–4 specific positives. Concrete observations, not flattery.

## What's not working
2–5 specific issues. Each one cites a layer. Brand Lock, Series Lock, Shot Spec, Composition, Technical, or Continuity.

## Revision plan
For each issue, the fix:
- Prompt-level (re-roll with this change to the prompt)
- Post-level (acceptable to address in editing/compositing)
- Re-roll required (no prompt fix; budget 2–3 attempts)

## Confidence
HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW, how sure you are about the verdict
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs

registros.texto: If only the image is provided with no context, ask for one piece of information: **what was this shot supposed to be?** A single sentence is enough to anchor the critique.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent

registros.texto:
What was this shot supposed to do? Pull from:

- Shot's `rationale` field (if shots.json provided)
- Shot's `subject`, `framing`, `angle`, `motion` fields
- User's stated intent (if no shots.json)
- The beat this shot serves

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent

registros.texto: If you can't establish intent in one sentence, ask. Don't critique blind.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer

registros.texto:
Read `references/critique-rubric.md` for the full rubric. Quick version, check the image against:

1. **Brand Lock**, does it respect palette, mood, "never" list?
2. **Series Lock**, does it match character/environment/lighting anchors?
3. **Shot Spec**, does framing/angle/composition match the spec?
4. **Composition**, does it reserve space for on-screen text if applicable?
5. **Technical**, skin texture, hands, eyes, anatomy, AI artifacts?
6. **Continuity**, if previous shots in the series are available, does it match?

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer

registros.texto: For each layer, note: pass / soft fail / hard fail. The verdict aggregates these.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes

registros.texto:
For every "not working" point, the critique must say what to do about it. Three buckets:

**Prompt-level fix**, change the prompt and re-roll. Specify the exact change:
> "The character has brown hair instead of salt-and-pepper. Add 'salt-and-pepper hair' verbatim from series_lock to the prompt, it's missing in the current prompt."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes

registros.texto:
**Post-level fix**, acceptable to address in compositing. Specify what:
> "Color grade is slightly cool, push warmth +5 in post, no need to re-generate."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes

registros.texto:
**Re-roll required**, no prompt fix will help; the generator just produced a bad sample. Budget 2–3 attempts:
> "Hands are mangled. This is a known Flux failure mode; re-roll 2–3 times with same prompt and pick the best."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict

registros.texto: | ACCEPT | All layers pass or soft-fail in ways post can fix |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence

registros.texto:
HIGH is a factual claim about what you had, not a mood. `tools/validate_critique.py`
rejects a `1.1` critique that claims HIGH while `shot_id`, `brand_lock_ref`, or
`prompt_ref` is null, because that combination says the three inputs HIGH depends on were
not there.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto:
After writing the markdown critique, **also** write
`output/critiques/round-{N}/{shot_id}.critique.json` conforming to
`templates/critique.schema.json` at version `1.1`. Same review, two surfaces. The markdown
is for the human; the JSON is so an automated QA loop (e.g. `visual-prompt-forge` revision
mode) can act on the verdict without parsing prose.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto:
Every one of those fields is required, and every one is nullable. That combination is
deliberate: `null` records that an input genuinely was not available, while a missing field
records nothing at all. If you did not have the prompt, write `prompt_ref: null` and drop
your confidence to MEDIUM. Do not omit the key.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto:
The hashes are the point. Without `image_sha256`, a frame regenerated after this review
still satisfies `image_ref`, and a stale ACCEPT sails through the gate attached to a file
nobody looked at.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto: **Severity, assign one per issue.** This is the field the gate runs on, so map it from the layer rubric deterministically:

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto: | `minor` | soft-fail, fixable in post | a soft-fail on any layer; `fix_type: post-level` |
registros.contexto:
| Severity | Means | Maps from |
|---|---|---|

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto: | `major` | hard-fail **with** a clear fix path | a hard-fail that a prompt change or re-roll fixes |
registros.contexto:
| Severity | Means | Maps from |
|---|---|---|

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto: | `blocking` | hard-fail on a critical layer (Brand Lock / Series Lock) with **no** clear fix, or a defect that makes the asset unusable | an unrecoverable hard-fail |
registros.contexto:
| Severity | Means | Maps from |
|---|---|---|

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto:
**Gating rule, the verdict is derived from severities, not chosen freely.** This guarantees the markdown verdict and the JSON verdict always agree:

- Any `blocking` issue ⇒ verdict is `REJECT`.
- Three or more `major` issues ⇒ verdict is `REJECT`.
- One or two `major` issues (and no blocking) ⇒ verdict is `REVISE`.
- Only `minor` issues, or none ⇒ verdict is `ACCEPT` (with post notes).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto:
The three-major rule used to read "escalate to REJECT at your discretion." Discretion in a
gate is not a gate, and it disagreed with `references/critique-rubric.md`, which called
three hard fails a REJECT outright. It is now a threshold, and the validator enforces it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

registros.texto: Pick the markdown `## Verdict` by this same rule.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate

registros.texto:
Writing a schema-valid critique is not the same as passing the gate. Run it:

```bash
python tools/validate_critique.py output/critiques/round-1/shot_03.critique.json
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate

registros.texto:
Or check the whole tree at once, which also recomputes every hash against the files on
disk:

```bash
python tools/validate_provenance.py output/
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate

registros.texto:
This step is not optional and it is not someone else's job. A critique that says `ACCEPT`
while carrying a `major` issue is a bug, and the only reason to write a validator for that
bug is to actually run it. Before this step existed, the gate ran in CI against two
fixtures that ship in the repo and never once against a real client's critique.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate

registros.texto:
Worked examples: `examples/critique.accept.json` and `examples/critique.revise.json` show
the shape at version `1.0`, which is still valid and carries no provenance.
`examples/worked-run/critiques/` shows version `1.1` with real hashes, two shots across two
rounds.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 1. No vibes-based critique

registros.texto: "Looks great" / "feels off" without specifics is not a critique. Every observation must reference something in the image (composition, color, anatomy, lighting direction, etc.).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 2. Prompt-level fixes must be specific

registros.texto: "Change the prompt" is not a fix. "Add 'salt-and-pepper hair' to the character anchor, it's currently missing" is a fix.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 3. Don't critique what wasn't asked

registros.texto: If the brief was "founder at laptop, calm mood" and the generation delivered exactly that, don't note that "the room could be more visually interesting." That's scope creep, not critique.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 4. Be honest about generator limits

registros.texto: Some failures (mangled hands, weird eye reflections, jewelry shimmer) are known generator weaknesses. Surface them as such, don't pretend a different prompt will fix them. Recommend re-roll or post.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 5. When in doubt, ACCEPT and recommend post

registros.texto: Generation is one stage in a pipeline. If the image is 80% right and the gap is fixable in post, that's an ACCEPT with post notes. Don't send the user back to re-generate when an editor would handle it in 90 seconds.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Example output

registros.texto:
> ## Verdict
> REVISE
>
> ## What's working
> - Composition correctly reserves the right two-thirds for text overlay (matches shot_03 rationale)
> - Lighting direction matches series_lock (window-left, warm afternoon)
> - Mood reads as calm/considered, on-brand
>
> ## What's not working
> - **Series Lock, character mismatch.** The character has brown hair, but series_lock specifies "salt-and-pepper." This is a verbatim-anchor failure.
> - **Technical, left hand.** Hand on the laptop has six fingers (Flux known failure mode).
> - **Shot Spec, framing.** Generated as MS but spec called for MCU. Subject is too small in frame.
>
> ## Revision plan
> - **Hair:** Prompt-level. Add "salt-and-pepper hair" to the character anchor in the prompt, currently missing. Re-roll.
> - **Hand:** Re-roll required. Generate 2–3 more times with same prompt and pick a clean one.
> - **Framing:** Prompt-level. Change "medium shot" to "medium close-up" in the prompt. Re-roll.
>
> ## Confidence
> HIGH

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Handoff

registros.texto:
After delivering the critique, if the verdict is REVISE, offer:

> "Want me to draft the revised prompt? Point `visual-prompt-forge` at this output tree in
> revision mode and it will re-emit prompts for just the shots that need them."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Handoff

registros.texto:
If the verdict is REJECT, do not offer that. REJECT means a blocking issue or three or more
major ones, which is a failure with no clear fix path, and revision mode is built to stop
there and ask. Say what blocked it and what decision it needs: a changed shot spec, a
changed brand-lock, or a different generator.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Handoff

registros.texto:
Don't auto-revise. The user picks. The critique you just wrote is exactly what closes that
loop.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric

registros.texto: The structured layer-by-layer pass. Use this as the checklist when reviewing a generated image.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 1. Brand Lock check

registros.texto: | Palette | Image colors come from brand-lock palette | Colors close but slightly off | Colors not in palette at all |
registros.contexto:
| Check | Pass | Soft fail | Hard fail |
|---|---|---|---|

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 1. Brand Lock check

registros.texto: | Mood adjectives | Image reads as the brand mood | Mood reads as adjacent (e.g. "calm" vs "neutral") | Image reads as a different mood (e.g. "energetic" when brief was "calm") |
registros.contexto:
| Check | Pass | Soft fail | Hard fail |
|---|---|---|---|

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 1. Brand Lock check

registros.texto: | "Never" list | None of the items in the never list are present | One item in the never list shows softly | Multiple never-list violations |
registros.contexto:
| Check | Pass | Soft fail | Hard fail |
|---|---|---|---|

registros.texto: | Aspect ratio | Matches `project.aspect` | Within a crop of the spec | Wrong aspect |
registros.contexto:
| Check | Pass | Soft fail | Hard fail |
|---|---|---|---|

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check

registros.texto: Technical hard fails are almost always **re-roll required**. The prompt was probably fine; the generator just produced a bad sample. Budget 2–3 re-rolls.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)

| Check | Pass | Soft fail | Hard fail |
|---|---|---|---|

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)

registros.texto: Continuity hard fails break the storyboard. REVISE with verbatim-anchor checks on the prompt.
